cell_type: human lung alveoli, human lung blood vessels

Micro-dissected morphologically normal human lung alveoli (0.082 mm3) and human lung blood vessels (0.094 mm3) from FFPE-fixed H&E-stained sections from Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) specimens (n–3 IPF specimens) were then subject to a qualitative and then quantitative proteomics approach using BayesENproteomics.
disease_state: The specimens used for this study met the criteria for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) diagnosis, however, we used distal lung tissue that appeared morphologically normal for the LCM-MS study.
material_type: Here we describe a microproteomics technique to analyse H&E-stained, formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues.
sample_source: The use of human lung tissue was approved by University of Manchester Health Research Authority with patient consent under protocol REC#14/NW/0260.
species: Laser capture microdissection coupled mass spectrometry (LCM-MS) for spatially resolved analysis of formalin-fixed and stained human lung tissues
tissue: Laser capture microdissection coupled mass spectrometry (LCM-MS) for spatially resolved analysis of formalin-fixed and stained human lung tissues
